[head=2][color=#9c1a00]The Crescent Recurrence[/color][/head]
The [bold]Crescent Recurrence[/bold], usually called [bold]the Turning[/bold], is a regional temporal instability. Moving reversion fronts pull exposed matter toward one of several previously stable physical states. They do not reset the whole sector or erase its political history.
The effect is strongest in low-gravity, recent, cheap, or poorly anchored places: asteroid belts, wreck clusters, temporary yards, forward laboratories, and improvised outposts. Stable planetary mass, mature stations, deep foundations, and expensive chronal anchors resist it.
[head=3][color=#9c1a00]Why Crescent stays valuable[/color][/head]
Ore moved out of an active basin and secured in stable space remains real. The exhausted field may later regain enough mass to be mined again. The Turning is not a clean duplication machine: seams shift, cycles restore different amounts, and deliberately exposed cargo is more likely to be erased or damaged than copied.
[head=3][color=#9c1a00]Knowledge does not reset[/color][/head]
Scientific theory, trained personnel, and protected records survive. What changes is Taypan's local phase environment. Advanced systems using recurrence-active materials, exotic energy states, or psionic interfaces must be tested and recalibrated for the current cycle. Outside laboratories can preserve theory; they cannot pre-calibrate a machine for conditions that do not exist until the new cycle settles.
[head=3][color=#9c1a00]Anchor Vaults[/color][/head]
Anchor Vaults protect certified records, identity templates, reference samples, and selected calibration baselines. They are expensive and limited. Major ports such as Edelheim, Chengridz, Gliess Santo, and Prometheus invest heavily in stability, so civilization continues while the operational frontier changes around it.
Forecasting services treat a Turning like severe weather: professionals can see a dangerous window approaching, but not exactly which compartment, asteroid, or prototype will revert.
